sw.B: Mimi ndimi Mzizi na Mzao wa Daudi, nyota ya asubuhi inayong'aa."
sw.R: Mimi ninatoka katika ukoo wa Daudi, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} ndiye ambaye ukoo wa Daudi ulitoka kwake. Mimi ni nyota ya asubuhi inayong'aa."

es.L: Yo soy la Raíz y el Linaje de David, la estrella resplandeciente de la mañana».
es.B: Yo soy la Raíz y el Descendiente de David, la brillante estrella de la mañana».
es.R: Yo vengo de la familia de David, y también soy aquel de quien vino la familia de David. Soy la brillante estrella de la mañana».

vi.L: Ta là Rễ và Dòng Dõi của Đa-vít, là Ngôi Sao Mai sáng chói."
vi.B: Ta là Rễ và Dòng Dõi của Đa-vít, là Ngôi Sao Mai sáng chói."
vi.R: Ta thuộc về dòng dõi Đa-vít, và Ta cũng là Đấng mà dòng dõi Đa-vít đến từ đó. Ta là ngôi sao mai sáng chói."

ko.L: 나는 다윗의 뿌리요 자손이며, 빛나는 새벽 별이다."
ko.B: 나는 다윗의 뿌리요 자손이며, 빛나는 새벽 별이다."
ko.R: 나는 다윗 집안에서 났고, 다윗 집안은 나에게서 시작되었다. 나는 빛나는 새벽 별이다."

pt.L: Eu sou a Raiz e a Descendência de Davi, a estrela brilhante da manhã."
pt.B: Eu sou a Raiz e o Descendente de Davi, a brilhante estrela da manhã."
pt.R: Eu venho da família de Davi, e também sou aquele de quem a família de Davi veio. Eu sou a brilhante estrela da manhã."

am.L: እኔ የዳዊት ሥርና ዘር፣ የሚያበራውም የንጋት ኮከብ ነኝ።»
am.B: እኔ የዳዊት ሥርና ዘር፣ የሚያበራው የንጋት ኮከብ ነኝ።»
am.R: እኔ ከዳዊት ቤተሰብ የመጣሁ ነኝ፤ የዳዊትም ቤተሰብ ከእኔ የመጣ ነው። የሚያበራው የንጋት ኮከብ እኔ ነኝ።»

decisions.choice: the Root and the Offspring of David
decisions.reason: See 5:5 and Isaiah 11:1, 10. Jesus is both David's descendant and the source from which David's line came.
See 2:28. "A star shall come out of Jacob" (Numbers 24:17). The morning star announces the dawn: Christ brings the day that has no night (22:5).
Titles of the Messiah are capitalized, as in 5:5.

decisions.choice: Mzizi na Mzao wa Daudi; nyota ya asubuhi
decisions.reason: "Mzizi" (root) as in 5:5, and "Mzao" (offspring, descendant), both capitalised as titles (m1); Readable explains the pair, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: la Raíz y el Linaje (L); la Raíz y el Descendiente (B)
decisions.reason: "Raíz" as in 5:5; the second word means offspring, family line, and Balanced names him as David's descendant.

decisions.choice: "Rễ và Dòng Dõi của Đa-vít", "Ngôi Sao Mai", capitalised (L, B)
decisions.reason: The Root of 5:5 and the morning star of 2:28 (m1, m2), now as titles Christ gives himself; Literal and Balanced capitalise them, as the English does, and Readable says what they mean.

decisions.choice: "다윗의 뿌리", as in 5:5; "자손"; "새벽 별", as in 2:28
decisions.reason: The Root and the Offspring of David and the bright morning star (meaning decisions); the Korean keeps 5:5's "다윗의 뿌리" and 2:28's "새벽 별". Korean has no capitals, so the titles stand as they are.

source.text: καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ νύμφη λέγουσιν· Ἔρχου· καὶ ὁ ἀκούων εἰπάτω· Ἔρχου· καὶ ὁ διψῶν ἐρχέσθω, ὁ θέλων λαβέτω ὕδωρ ζωῆς δωρεάν.

records.literal_gloss: And the Spirit and the bride say: Come. And the [one] hearing let him say: Come. And the [one] thirsting let him come, the [one] wishing let him take water of life freely.

en.L: And the Spirit and the bride say, "Come!" And let the one who hears say, "Come!" And let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who wishes take the water of life freely.
en.B: The Spirit and the bride say, "Come!" And whoever hears should say, "Come!" Whoever is thirsty should come; whoever wants it should take the water of life, free of charge.
en.R: The Spirit and the bride say, "Come!" Everyone who hears this should say, "Come!" Anyone who is thirsty may come. Anyone who wants the water of life may take it as a free gift.

fr.L: Et l’Esprit et la mariée disent : « Viens ! » Et que celui qui entend dise : « Viens ! » Et que celui qui a soif vienne ; que celui qui veut prenne de l’eau de vie gratuitement.
fr.B: L’Esprit et la mariée disent : « Viens ! » Que celui qui entend dise aussi : « Viens ! » Que celui qui a soif vienne ; que celui qui le désire prenne l’eau de la vie, gratuitement.
fr.R: L’Esprit et la mariée disent : « Viens ! » Que tous ceux qui entendent cela disent : « Viens ! » Tous ceux qui ont soif peuvent venir. Tous ceux qui veulent l’eau de la vie peuvent la prendre, comme un cadeau.

sw.L: Na Roho na bibi arusi wanasema, "Njoo!" Na yeye asikiaye na aseme, "Njoo!" Na yeye aliye na kiu na aje; yeye atakaye na ayatwae maji ya uzima bure.
sw.B: Roho na bibi arusi wanasema, "Njoo!" Na kila anayesikia na aseme, "Njoo!" Kila mwenye kiu na aje; kila anayetaka na ayachukue maji ya uzima bila malipo.
sw.R: Roho na bibi arusi wanasema, "Njoo!" Kila anayesikia haya na aseme, "Njoo!" Mtu yeyote mwenye kiu anaweza kuja. Mtu yeyote anayetaka maji ya uzima anaweza kuyachukua kama zawadi ya bure.

es.L: Y el Espíritu y la novia dicen: «¡Ven!». Y el que oye, diga: «¡Ven!». Y el que tiene sed, venga; el que quiera, tome gratuitamente el agua de la vida.
es.B: El Espíritu y la novia dicen: «¡Ven!». Y el que oiga, diga: «¡Ven!». El que tenga sed, venga; y el que quiera, tome gratuitamente el agua de la vida.
es.R: El Espíritu y la novia dicen: «¡Ven!». Todo el que oiga esto, diga: «¡Ven!». El que tenga sed, puede venir. El que quiera el agua de la vida, puede tomarla como un regalo.

vi.L: Và Thánh Linh và cô dâu nói: "Hãy đến!" Và ai nghe, hãy nói: "Hãy đến!" Và ai khát, hãy đến; ai muốn, hãy nhận lấy nước sự sống cách nhưng không.
vi.B: Thánh Linh và cô dâu nói: "Xin hãy đến!" Ai nghe thì hãy nói: "Xin hãy đến!" Ai khát thì hãy đến; ai muốn thì hãy nhận lấy nước sự sống mà không phải trả tiền.
vi.R: Thánh Linh và cô dâu nói: "Xin hãy đến!" Ai nghe điều này cũng hãy nói: "Xin hãy đến!" Ai khát thì có thể đến. Ai muốn nước sự sống thì có thể nhận lấy như một món quà, không phải trả gì cả.

ko.L: 그리고 성령과 신부가 "오십시오!" 하고 말한다. 그리고 듣는 사람도 "오십시오!" 하고 말하여라. 그리고 목마른 사람은 오너라. 원하는 사람은 생명수를 값없이 받아라.
ko.B: 성령과 신부가 "오십시오!" 하고 말한다. 듣는 사람도 "오십시오!" 하고 말하여라. 목마른 사람은 오너라. 원하는 사람은 누구나 생명수를 값없이 받아라.
ko.R: 성령과 신부가 "오십시오!" 하고 말한다. 이 말씀을 듣는 사람은 누구나 "오십시오!" 하고 말하여라. 목마른 사람은 누구나 오너라. 생명수를 원하는 사람은 누구나 그것을 값없이 받아라.

pt.L: E o Espírito e a noiva dizem: "Vem!" E quem ouve diga: "Vem!" E quem tem sede venha; quem quiser receba de graça a água da vida.
pt.B: O Espírito e a noiva dizem: "Vem!" E quem ouvir diga: "Vem!" Quem tiver sede, venha; quem quiser, receba a água da vida sem nada pagar.
pt.R: O Espírito e a noiva dizem: "Vem!" Todos os que ouvirem isto devem dizer: "Vem!" Quem tiver sede pode vir. Quem quiser a água da vida pode recebê-la como um presente.

decisions.choice: Come! A prayer to Christ, and then an invitation
alternatives: all three are invitations to the hearers
decisions.reason: The Spirit and the bride, the church, call to Christ to come, answering his "I am coming" (22:12, 20), and every hearer is to join the prayer. Then the call turns outward: whoever is thirsty is invited to come and drink. Some read the first two calls also as invitations to the hearers.

decisions.choice: the water of life freely: Isaiah 55:1
decisions.reason: See 21:6. The book that warns so sternly ends with an open invitation.
The Greek command is singular, a prayer to Christ to come, as the meaning decision says; "ven" addressed to him takes no span, being a verb form.

"Come!" is a prayer to Christ, then an invitation (m1); Balanced and Readable add "xin", which makes it a respectful plea to him, and the invitation that follows keeps the plain "hãy". "Nhưng không" as in 21:6.

decisions.choice: "오십시오!" (합쇼체) for the first two cries; "오너라" for the thirsty
decisions.reason: Come! is a prayer to Christ, and then an invitation, uncertain (meaning decision); Korean must choose a speech level for each, so the first two take the form of prayer to Christ, as in 22:20, and the third is spoken to the thirsty in the plain imperative.
The water of life freely echoes Isaiah 55:1 (meaning decision), and is worded as in 21:6.

The first two calls are a prayer to Christ to come (m1), so they use the "tu" imperative "Vem", as "Vem, Senhor Jesus" in 22:20 and "Nosso Senhor, vem!" in 1 Corinthians 16:22; the invitation to the thirsty turns to the third person "venha", "receba", and Portuguese shows the shift that English "come" hides.
The cry "Come!" is addressed to the coming Lord, one person; as everywhere in this translation, people speak to Jesus with the familiar singular (አንተ), so ና is used here and in the prayer of 22:20.

decisions.choice: do not add or take away: Deuteronomy 4:2
decisions.reason: Moses warned Israel not to add to God's commands or take away from them (Deuteronomy 4:2; 12:32). The warning protects this prophecy from being changed or distorted by those who copy and teach it.
"I" may be Jesus, who "testifies to these things" (22:20), or John, the book's witness (22:8). Either way the warning carries Christ's authority.
As in 1:11, the book is a scroll at every level.
Spanish "le" serves for man or woman, so the English gender span has no Spanish counterpart.

The meaning decision leaves open whether Jesus or John speaks (m2), but Vietnamese must choose a pronoun. The next verses name "the one who testifies to these things" as Jesus (22:20), so Vietnamese gives him "Ta"; "tôi" would choose John. A reviewer should weigh this choice.

decisions.choice: "나는 ... 증언한다", first person in the plain style, without naming the speaker; no gender spans
decisions.reason: Do not add or take away echoes Deuteronomy 4:2 (meaning decision). Whether "I testify" is Jesus or John is uncertain (meaning decision); Korean "나" with the plain verb fits either, as Jesus and John both speak so in this book.

Spanish follows the text the English follows, as the footnoted meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: Come, Lord Jesus: the prayer of the early church
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the Aramaic prayer "Marana tha", "Our Lord, come!" (1 Corinthians 16:22), and it was used in early Christian worship. John answers Christ's promise with the church's prayer.
The prayer of the early church (m1), in the forms of prayer to the Lord: "Lạy" and "xin". With "Chúa", the honorific "Đức" is not used.

decisions.choice: "주 예수님, 오십시오!" in 합쇼체, as a prayer
decisions.reason: Come, Lord Jesus, is the prayer of the early church (meaning decision); Korean prayer to the Lord takes 합쇼체 and "님", as the songs of this book address God and the Lamb, and as in 22:17.

The prayer speaks to Jesus, so it uses "tu" (style section 4): "vem" is the "tu" imperative, as in the Portuguese of 1 Corinthians 16:22 ("Nosso Senhor, vem!"), whose Aramaic prayer this echoes (m1). The Greek has no Aramaic word here, so "Maranata" is not used.

decisions.choice: ጌታ ኢየሱስ ሆይ፣ ና (Come, Lord Jesus), at every level
decisions.reason: The address keeps ጌታ ... ሆይ, the style brief's form for "Lord!" at every level, so the prayer reads alike in all three; the verb is the familiar singular, as in 22:17.
